0.0.n: A brief opening acknowledgment before the greeting.

0.2.n: A standard daytime greeting, suitable for a polite introduction.

0.4.n: Part of the English name The Game Gallery.

0.6.n: Part of the English name The Game Gallery, not a separate Japanese word.

0.8.n: Completes the English name The Game Gallery.

0.9.n: Links the channel name to the speaker, showing affiliation.

0.10.n: The name portion of the speaker's handle, Haru99.

0.11.n: These digits complete the speaker's handle, Haru99.

0.12.n: A polite sentence ending; the speaker leaves out 私, meaning I.

1.0.n: Sets the time for the planned introduction.

1.1.n: Adds a friendly conversational pause after 今日.

1.3.n: ご adds politeness to 紹介; したい expresses the speaker's desire to do it.

1.4.n: An English-derived word described by the preceding phrase ご紹介したい.

1.5.n: Marks the item as the topic about which the speaker gives information.

1.6.n: Politely points to the item being shown; the usual ending です is omitted.

2.0.n: Refers to an earlier occasion when the game was introduced.

2.1.n: Marks 以前 as the time of the earlier introduction.

2.2.n: In ですね here, です creates a polite pause rather than a separate statement.

2.3.n: Combines with です to hold the listener's attention during a pause.

2.5.n: Emphasizes that the introduction has happened before now.

2.6.n: ご紹介しております uses humble おる instead of いる, politely referring to the speaker's own earlier introduction.

3.1.n: Names the people living there; Japanese does not explicitly mark singular or plural here.

3.2.n: Marks 裏切り者 as the subject of 住む inside a phrase describing 丘; が could serve this role too.

3.3.n: The plain form directly describes 丘: the hill where the traitors live.

3.4.n: The noun described by 裏切り者の住む in this Japanese game title.

3.5.n: Links 丘 to 上 to indicate the hill's top.

3.6.n: In 丘の上, identifies the location above or atop the hill.

3.7.n: Links 丘の上 to 館, describing where the mansion is located.

3.8.n: Refers to a large house and completes the Japanese game title.

3.10.n: Politely identifies the previously introduced game by its title.

3.11.n: Softens the identification and invites the listener to follow along.

4.1.n: The opening word of the game's English title.

4.3.n: An English location word within the game title, not a Japanese particle.

4.5.n: An English noun within the game's title.

4.7.n: Part of the English title, locating the house atop the hill.

4.9.n: The English article before Hill within the game title.

4.11.n: The final word of the game's English title.

4.13.n: Adds a polite Japanese ending after the English title.

4.14.n: Connects politely to what follows; here it introduces more information rather than a strong contrast.

5.0.n: Refers back to the game just named, rather than a direction.

5.1.n: Links the game to its expansion set, despite the intervening conversational pause.

5.2.n: Part of the hesitation ですね, inserted before the speaker continues with 拡張セット.

5.3.n: Helps maintain a friendly conversational flow during the pause.

5.5.n: Combines with セット to describe additional content for the existing game.

5.6.n: An English-derived noun forming 拡張セット with the preceding word.

5.7.n: Marks the expansion set as the thing that has come out.

5.8.n: 出ておりまして is a formal, polite linking form of 出ている, describing a release and continuing the sentence.

6.0.n: Refers back to the expansion set mentioned in the preceding line.

6.1.n: Marks それ as what the speaker is now identifying.

6.2.n: Points politely to the expansion being shown.

6.3.n: Politely links the previously mentioned expansion to the item on display.

6.4.n: Softens the identification while directing the listener's attention to the item.

6.7.n: Begins the base game's English title, repeated to identify which game the expansion belongs to.

6.9.n: An English location word within the base game's title.

6.11.n: Part of the base game's English title, not a Japanese word.

6.13.n: Locates the house relative to the hill within the English title.

6.15.n: The English article used before Hill in the game title.

6.17.n: Completes the base game's English title.

6.19.n: Connects the base game to its named expansion, Widow's Walk.

6.21.n: Part of the expansion name Widow's Walk, an English term for a rooftop viewing platform.

6.23.n: This s belongs to English 's in Widow's, not to Japanese grammar.

6.25.n: Completes the expansion name Widow's Walk; the full phrase refers to a rooftop viewing platform.

6.27.n: Politely finishes the identification of the expansion by name.

6.28.n: Adds a friendly, lightly confirming tone to the sentence ending.

0.lit: Okay, hello. [I] am The Game Gallery's Haru99.
0.tip: の can show affiliation: The Game GalleryのHaru99 identifies Haru99 as belonging to that channel.

1.lit: Today, you know, the item [I] want to introduce—as for it, this one.
1.tip: ご紹介したい comes before アイテム, so it describes the item the speaker wants to introduce.

2.lit: Previously, you know, [I] have already introduced [it],
2.tip: ご紹介しております politely describes the speaker's own introduction, here understood as something already done.

3.lit: [It] is the mansion on top of the hill where traitors live, you know.
3.tip: The first の marks who lives there; the later の particles link the hill, its top, and the mansion.

4.lit: [It] is Betrayal at House on the Hill, though,
4.tip: けども often serves as a gentle bridge to the next point without implying a strong but.

5.lit: For this one, you know, an expansion set has come out, and,
5.tip: 出る means come out here, so 出ておりまして reports a release while politely connecting to the next statement.

6.lit: That is this one, you see: Betrayal at House on the Hill's Widow's Walk, you know.
6.tip: それ refers back to the expansion already mentioned, while こちら points to the item now being shown.
